fields.v: Kozyrev, M., Kozyrev, A., Podkopaev, A. (2026). Skill Issue: Lessons from Optimizing Repository SKILLs for Coding Agents. arXiv:2609.12742v1 [cs.AI], 11 Sep 2026
Preprint — arXiv; footer 'Preprint.', no venue in the arXiv metadata
JetBrains Research (all); Technical University of Munich (M. Kozyrev); Constructor University Bremen (Podkopaev)

Compares; secondary: Proposes an evaluation method — SKILL.md documents produced by two optimizers (GEPA, SkillOpt) vs an empty seed SKILL, same agent and model, three Kotlin repositories; evaluation method: reverse-PR task mining at a single frozen base commit + paired rollout objective
fields.why: Judgement: contribution (i) is the reverse-PR mining pipeline with the paired objective (p. 3), so 'Proposes an evaluation method' as main nature is also defensible; reading the mining + optimization pipeline as a proposed approach for SKILL synthesis would make Q13 apply
fields.doubt: A contribuição (i) é o pipeline de mineração de PRs revertidos com a métrica emparelhada (p. 3). Decide se a natureza principal é Compares ou Proposes an evaluation method, e se conta como abordagem proposta (afeta Q13).

fields.v: Not an SDD approach. Repository SKILL (single SKILL.md loaded into agent context, agentskills.io / Anthropic SKILL spec), synthesized automatically by GEPA (Agrawal et al., 2025; 200 scored attempts) and SkillOpt (Yang et al., 2026; 3 epochs). Versions Not stated
One SKILL.md per repository (repository knowledge: module layout, build/test commands, conventions, e.g. multiplatform source-set rules, module registration); seed = empty document (header only)

Optimization loop: run agent with candidate SKILL on mined tasks -> reflect over trajectories -> propose edits -> keep if paired score improves on validation; final SKILL evaluated on held-out test split
None in the loop; post-hoc maintainer review of the koog SKILLs and of blinded patches; authors recommend reviewing any generated SKILL before merge
Single artefact (SKILL.md context file)
Not classifiable (authors' wording: 'repository knowledge', 'plain .md files versioned alongside the code')
Existing code bases: merged pull requests reverted at a frozen base commit (bug fixes and features), plus two open issues in koog
koog 119 tasks (from 660 PRs), ktor 131 (from 452), kotest 100 (sampled); held-out test splits 20-26 tasks (69 pooled); median task size 54 lines/3 files (koog), 27/2 (ktor), 16/1 (kotest)
Kotlin/JVM open-source libraries: kotest (testing), ktor (web framework), koog (agentic framework, JetBrains)
N/A (no human participants; one koog maintainer as reviewer)
Agent API spend per optimization run (USD), wall-clock hours; mean $0.84 per rollout; cost and API/wall time per live issue
Resolved tasks (all hidden FAIL_TO_PASS tests pass, regression guards); paired score vs seed rollout (0.5 = no change)
Maintainer's qualitative reading of patches (minimalism, tidiness, strange comments); diff size as tie-breaker
None
Task mining yield; maintainer judgment of SKILL content; honesty of final claim and test-file edits (in paired objective); sign-test detectable effect size

Automatic: hidden tests in per-repo Docker images, paired comparison of rollouts (test-file edits/false claims, F2P, then fraction passed, honesty, diff size, tool calls), sign test. Manual: one maintainer reviewed SKILLs and anonymized patches

Agent: Claude Code + Sonnet 4.6 (frozen) for all. Authors' criterion for an optimized SKILL: paired score vs the empty-seed rollout on the held-out split must beat 0.5 ('the number a candidate has to beat', p. 5), with a sign test at p=0.05 to attribute the gain to the document (p. 7); also reported: resolved tasks (all hidden FAIL_TO_PASS tests pass). No cost criterion stated. Per-configuration run cost on the held-out split not reported; mean $0.84 per rollout over all runs.
- Empty seed SKILL (baseline, Claude Code + Sonnet 4.6): resolves 40% koog, 51% kotest, 66% ktor (53% pooled); held-out 14/23, 13/20, 16/26; paired score 0.5 by definition. Quality: no criterion stated by the authors; cost: no criterion stated by the authors
- GEPA SKILL, koog: paired 0.525; 14 -> 15 of 23; optimization spend $368.82, 4.7 h. Quality: partly (beats 0.5, sign test n.s.); cost: no criterion stated by the authors
- GEPA SKILL, kotest: 0.554; 13 -> 16 of 20; $182.48, 4.9 h. Quality: partly (beats 0.5, n.s.); cost: no criterion stated by the authors
- GEPA SKILL, ktor: 0.567; 16 -> 20 of 26; $312.87, 13.0 h. Quality: partly (beats 0.5, n.s.); cost: no criterion stated by the authors
- SkillOpt SKILL, koog: 0.546; +2 tasks; $401.44, 8.14 h. Quality: partly (beats 0.5, n.s.); cost: no criterion stated by the authors
- SkillOpt SKILL, kotest: 0.519; +1; $263.56, 13.3 h. Quality: partly (beats 0.5, n.s.); cost: no criterion stated by the authors
- SkillOpt SKILL, ktor: 0.437; -2; $484.81, 25.2 h. Quality: does not work (below 0.5); cost: no criterion stated by the authors
- (Best sign test over all runs p = 0.29; none clears p = 0.05)
- Live koog issues #1275/#1354, no SKILL: $6.06/$4.85, API 8m21s/7m21s, wall 14m59s/20m29s; maintainer: 'does a bit extra', 'strange comments' (#1275), 'overall ok' (#1354); no integration test. Quality: no criterion stated by the authors; cost: no criterion stated by the authors
- Live koog issues, GEPA SKILL: $2.48/$3.10, API 3m35s/4m52s, wall 5m32s/7m38s; maintainer: 'notably more minimalist', 'a bit tidier'; no integration test. Quality: no criterion stated by the authors; cost: no criterion stated by the authors
- Live koog issues, SkillOpt SKILL: $2.44/$4.20, API 3m43s/5m33s, wall 5m30s/8m24s; maintainer: 'looks fine', 'almost identical' to GEPA; no integration test. Quality: no criterion stated by the authors; cost: no criterion stated by the authors
- Ablation (preliminary tracy sweep, Tables 3-4, generic-checklist seed): rejected objectives binary resolve, gold match, token price, judge, file scores; most shipped no file or overfit; not part of the reported results
fields.why: Round 2 gave verdicts from the extractor's own cut-offs: seed 'partly (about half resolved)', cost 'works'/'partly'/'does not work' from spend size, live-issue 'works' from maintainer remarks; the paper states no criterion for any of these, so per the 2026-11-23 rule they become 'no criterion stated by the authors' (a correction). Kept quality verdicts only for the optimized SKILLs, because the authors state that 0.5 is 'the number a candidate has to beat' (p. 5) and test attribution with a sign test at p=0.05 (p. 7): above 0.5 but n.s. = partly, below 0.5 = does not work. Whether that counts as a stated success criterion is the open point. Values unchanged (Table 1 p. 6, Table 2 p. 12, pp. 6-7)
fields.doubt: Os autores dizem que 0,5 é 'o número a bater' e usam um sign test a p=0,05; mantive partly/does not work só para os SKILLs otimizados. Decide se isto conta como critério de sucesso ou se todos passam a 'no criterion stated by the authors'.

fields.v: Tasks: reverse-PR mined tasks per repository split once into train/validation/test; GEPA 200 scored attempts, SkillOpt 3 epochs on same splits. Configurations: empty seed, GEPA SKILL, SkillOpt SKILL. Baseline: empty SKILL. Held constant: agent (Claude Code), model (Sonnet 4.6), tools, limits, Docker image, frozen base without .git. Acceptance tests: hidden FAIL_TO_PASS tests + up to 30 regression guards. Repetitions: seed run once per task; one candidate rollout per task. Human intervention: none

GEPA +4.9 pp mean (wins on all 3 repos); SkillOpt +0.1 pp (loss on ktor cancels gains). Not significant: best sign test p = 0.29; at 20-26 tasks detectable only if document wins 4 of 5 disagreements (2 of 3 pooled over 69). Maintainer would take GEPA SKILL 'as a draft'; with either SKILL live issues solved in under half the time and at lower cost (2 issues, single runs). Total optimization spend $2,013.98, 69.2 h

No (on the score): paired metric could not separate gains from agent run-to-run variance at feasible split sizes; reverse mining at frozen base fixed stale-claim SKILLs from forward mining. Limitations stated: few tasks per repository, cost per rollout, LLM reverter defects (static check rejected 56 of 280), single maintainer

At least 100 graded tasks needed and still too few for significance; two repositories (tracy, http4k) failed to reach the floor; LLM reverter introduces defects; one maintainer of one repository; Kotlin only. Future: cheaper rollouts, evaluation not based on pass rate, developer study with many reviewers
